newsitem.title: BELARUS: Police briefly detain 14 journalists in Belarus.
newsitem.headline: Police briefly detain 14 journalists in Belarus.

text.p: Belarussian police on Thursday briefly detained 14 journalists in the capital Minsk who were taking part in and reporting on the handing in of a petition in support of an arrested Russian television crew, witnesses said.

A Reuters correspondent was among those detained and filed a brief report by telephone from the building where he was being held. Other reporters and cameramen from Belarussian and foreign media were also detained.
They were later released and will face court on Friday morning on charges of violating a decree by President Alexander Lukashenko, who had imposed tough restrictions on public rallies.

Several dozen reporters staged a protest demanding the release of a crew from Public Russian Television (ORT) who face up to five years in prison after authorities charged them with illegally crossing the Belarussian-Lithuanian border.
Journalists picketed Minsk's KGB security service building and the Interior Ministry before moving to the headquarters of the administration of hardline Lukashenko.

Police closed in on both the protesting journalists and reporters covering the action as the protesters tried to hand in their petition to Lukashenko's office. One witness said one correspondent was beaten by police.
Journalists have frequently been detained in Minsk during opposition rallies, but often they are quickly fined and released.
The detention of the ORT crew at the weekend sparked a war of words between Moscow and Minsk and a protest from human rights group Amnesty International.
Russian President Boris Yeltsin threatened to review a union treaty he signed with Lukashenko just four months ago.
Lukashenko reacted "with surprise and astonishment", saying Yeltsin must have been misled by his advisers. His press service accused the journalists of being part of a deliberate plot.
On Thursday he accused the detained ORT correspondent, Pavel Sheremet, of being in the pay of foreign intelligence services but did not name them.
